newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CRAWL TO 59-3 AGAINST SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CRAWL TO 59-3 AGAINST SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Australia struggled grimly to 59 for three wickets at lunch on the second day of the second test in Port Elizabeth on Saturday. Just 49 runs were scored in the session.
Resuming at 10 for one, the tourists lost captain Mark Taylor in the third over of the morning to a thin edge off Shaun Pollock which 'keeper Dave Richardson caught diving to his left.

Taylor, who added just one run to his overnight seven, extended his thoroughly miserable run of form to 17 consecutive test innings without a half century. His awkward stay at the crease lasted 67 minutes and 44 balls but could have ended at any stage
But the wicket was a bitter-sweet success for South Africa as Pollock limped off the field with a strained left hamstring after bowling just two overs and will not be able to bowl again in the test.

Mark Waugh briefly flattered to deceive in a 36 ball innings of 20 that included three typically elegant boundaries. But he became the third wicket to fall when a Hansie Cronje inswinger trapped him lbw with the total on 48.

Matthew Elliott showed commendable spirit and determination to survive a fierce 10 over spell from Allan Donald which saw the 25-year-old Victorian left hander hit three times on the shoulder and in the ribs.
But his obduracy was what Australia needed and he was still there at lunch unbeaten on 22 from 115 balls. Steve Waugh was three not out.
